chunks: He, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, forbade jidad at night, meaning the jidad of palm trees. Jidad is the cutting/harvesting. He forbade it at night because the poor do not attend it.

key_terms.الْجَدَادِ: Harvesting or cracking open palm fruit clusters

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet forbid night harvesting of palm trees?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights that the prohibition of night harvesting (jidad) was primarily a social safeguard to ensure the poor could witness and claim their share of the produce, preventing the wealthy from concealing yields. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on economic justice and transparency in agricultural transactions, linking the physical act of cutting the fruit clusters to the broader ethical obligation of community welfare.
